scope: Independent read-only audit of lesson mathematics, displayed figure values, demo numerical claims, all ten Exercise/Solution pairs, and exact local source routes.

summary.reason: All displayed DFT values, signed-bin labels, normalization and Parseval factors, real-input even/odd boundaries, circular-convolution results, padding condition, zero-padding claims, exercise solutions, figure ledgers, demo thresholds, and cited local source routes are correct and mutually consistent.

method.independent_recomputation: Direct complex-exponential sums and modulo-index convolution were recomputed independently from the lesson. The demo spectrum, local-maximum threshold, target-frequency tolerance, valley test, and both phase cases were independently reproduced from the frozen parameters.
method.rounding: The off-bin DFT was checked before rounding and agrees with the lesson to six decimals.
method.conventions_used: Unscaled negative-sign forward DFT, positive-sign 1/N inverse, unshifted k=0,...,N-1 storage, and the signed half-open interval [-f_s/2,f_s/2).

checks.evidence: The declared forward/inverse pair and W_N=e^{-j2pi/N} agree. Roots-of-unity orthogonality is stated for positive integer N and yields exact inversion with the 1/N factor.
For cos(2pi(2/8)n), direct summation gives X[2]=X[6]=4 and zero elsewhere; k=6 is the -2 representative modulo 8.
delta[n] gives X[k]=1 for every bin, and N=1 reduces to X[0]=x[0]. The same N correctly governs both coordinate sets.
For x=[1,0,-1,0], the basis rows and DftBasisCorrelations figure give X=[0,2,0,2]; the displayed n=2 inverse value is -1 and the complete inverse is exact.
For x=[1,0,1,0], direct row correlations give X=[2,0,2,0], and the n=1 inverse check is (2+2e^{jpi})/4=0.
At N=8 and f_s=8 kHz, delta-f=1 kHz and the signed labels are [0,+1,+2,+3,-4,-3,-2,-1] kHz. The SVG and RealDftConventionLedger use the same endpoint convention.
At N=6 and f_s=12 kHz, unshifted labels are [0,2,4,6,8,10] kHz and signed labels are [0,+2,+4,-6,-4,-2] kHz; k=3 is the unique Nyquist singleton.
The k<N/2 versus k>=N/2 rule retains 0 through (N-1)/2 for odd N. Even N has one Nyquist coordinate labeled -f_s/2 here; odd N has no Nyquist bin.
The distinction between first-to-last span (N-1)T_s and periodized aperture NT_s is correct, and f_s/N=1/(NT_s) follows.
For real x, X[(N-k) mod N]=X*[k]. DC is real, even-N Nyquist is real, and all non-singleton retained odd-N bins have distinct conjugate partners.
For N=8, cos(2pi n/8) gives X[1]=X[7]=4. Adding phase pi/3 gives 4e^{+jpi/3} and 4e^{-jpi/3}; inverse contributions each have complex-exponential amplitude 1/2.

Independent real-input bins are 0 through floor(N/2). The amplitude rule |X|/N at DC and even-N Nyquist and 2|X|/N at paired interior bins is correct; the figure's A[1]=1 and scale rows 4, 1/2, and sqrt(2) are correct for the N=8 cosine.
For 2+3cos(2pi(2/8)n-pi/4)+(-1)^n, the nonzero raw bins are X[0]=16, X[2]=12e^{-jpi/4}, X[4]=8, X[6]=12e^{+jpi/4}; one-sided amplitudes are 2, 3, and 1 with only k=2 doubled.

For x[n]=(-1)^n and N=8, raw X[4]=8, unitary X_u[4]=sqrt(8), and forward-scaled X_f[4]=1. Exact round-trip scaling requires alpha beta N=1; N/2 is correctly restricted to a paired real sinusoid's raw bin magnitude.
The course identity sum|x[n]|^2=(1/N)sum|X[k]|^2 follows from the declared pair. The alternating record checks as 8=(1/8)64 and the unitary check is |sqrt(8)|^2=8.
For X_alpha=alpha X, time energy equals (1/(N|alpha|^2))sum|X_alpha|^2. For x=[1,0,-1,0], both sides equal 2; unitary alpha makes the prefactor one.
The modulo-N definition is correct. The substitution r=(n-m) mod N is a permutation and proves DFT{x circledast_N h}=XH under the course pair.
For x=[1,2], h=[1,-1], linear convolution is [1,1,-2]; wrapping index 2 modulo 2 gives [-1,1], while padding to N=3 preserves [1,1,-2].
For x=[1,2,3], h=[1,1], linear convolution is [1,3,5,3], N=3 circular convolution is [4,3,5], and N=4 reproduces the linear result.
For x=[2,-1], h=[1,3,2], linear convolution is [2,5,1,-2], N=3 circular convolution is [0,5,1], and the smallest guaranteed declared-array length is N=4.

For arrays beginning at zero with declared lengths L_x and L_h, N>=L_x+L_h-1 is the correct alias-free implementation guarantee. The wording appropriately describes allocated length; shorter actual support from endpoint zeros would only relax the minimum.

Appending zeros to length L evaluates the unchanged N-term finite-record DTFT at 2pi k/L. It changes grid spacing from f_s/N to f_s/L but adds no acquired data and cannot narrow the record-limited response.

At f_s=1024 Hz, N=64 gives 16 Hz original spacing. The largest displayed sample for the 173 Hz tone is 176 Hz at Q=1 and Q=2, error 3/16=0.1875 original bins; Q=4 first moves it to 172 Hz, error 1/16=0.0625, satisfying the strict <0.1 target.

With L=1024 the grid is 1 Hz in both comparisons. At N=64, phase 0 has one candidate maximum at 171 Hz and phase 90 has maxima at 166 and 187 Hz, so the target-pair test fails. At N=256, both phases have distinct target maxima at exactly 170 and 180 Hz with an intervening valley, so both pass. The 32 Hz versus 8 Hz rectangular null-to-null widths and 62.5 ms versus 250 ms apertures in PaddingDurationResolution are correct.
The N=4 closing table correctly maps X=[0,2,0,2] to [0,+2,-4,-2] kHz and reconstructs [1,0,-1,0].

The N=1, constant, even-N alternating, and odd-N truncated-alternating cases apply singleton/doubling rules correctly. For cos(2pi(1.5/8)n), the independently computed bins are (1,0), (1,2.179580427), (1,-2.613125930), (1,-0.648846698), (1,0), and their conjugates, so every bin is nonzero as claimed.

The phase-sensitive versus amplitude-report choice, inverse check, and factor-of-two rule are correct. The radix-two split correctly defines four-point E and O, uses W_8^{k+4}=-W_8^k with four-periodic E,O, and obtains X[k+4]=E[k]-W_8^kO[k].
